label: Paralleled Enlightenment feminist critiques of women’s artificial miseducation in colonial Bengal
description: Like Wollstonecraft’s critique of gendered sensibility, Begum Rokeya exposed how domestic confinement (aborodh) deliberately atrophies women’s rational faculties.
dialecticalTension: Translates feminist rationalism into an anti-colonial Bengali Muslim social context.
historicalContext: Early 20th-century Bengal Renaissance and Muslim women’s reform.

label: Continued 19th-century Indian women’s structural critique of domestic seclusion and illiteracy
description: Following Ramabai’s institutional battles for women’s schools in western India, Rokeya founded the Sakhawat Memorial Girls’ School in Calcutta in 1911.
dialecticalTension: Advances cross-community South Asian women’s educational emancipation.

label: Anticipated feminist historiography of patriarchal seclusion and domestic ideology in South Asia
description: Rokeya’s sharp material analysis of purdah and unequal intellectual labor laid foundational groundwork for later Indian feminist sociology.
dialecticalTension: Connects early 20th-century anti-seclusion critique to contemporary structural gender history.
